title: C# Questions & Answers - Fundamentals of Class
sourceFile: Class Fundamentals - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on fundamentals of class in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: sample.fun(1, 5) will set value 5 in arr[1]

questions.explanation: The method 'fun' is an instance method (non-static). In C#, instance methods must be called through an object reference ('s.fun'), not through the class name ('sample.fun'). Attempting to call it via the class name results in a compile-time error.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to define the member of a class externally in C#?
questions.explanation: Unlike C++, C# does not allow members of a class to be defined outside of the class body using a scope resolution operator. All members (methods, fields, etc.) must be defined within the class definition.

questions.question: Which operator is used to access the member functions of a class?
questions.explanation: In C#, the dot operator (.) is used to access members (fields, properties, and methods) of an object instance or static members of a class.

questions.question: What is primarily specified using a class declaration in C#?
questions.explanation: A class declaration defines a new reference type and creates a local scope for the members defined within that class.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The 'this' keyword refers to the current instance of the class. Inside 'fun(10, 20)', 'this.i = i' sets the class field 'i' to 10, and 'this.j = j' sets it to 20.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about objects in C# is correct?

options.text: Almost everything in C# is an object or inherits from System.Object
Objects have members (methods, properties, events) that perform actions

questions.explanation: In C#, objects are the building blocks of applications. They are instances of classes and follow the unified type system where everything derives from System.Object.

questions.question: Which mechanism binds together code and data, keeping both safe from outside interference?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation is an OOP principle that bundles data (fields) and the methods that operate on that data into a single unit (class) and restricts direct access to some of the object's components.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to declare and instantiate an object for a class named 'name'?
questions.explanation: In C#, the standard way to create an object is to specify the type, the variable name, and the 'new' keyword followed by the constructor.

questions.question: By default, the data members of a class in C# are:
questions.explanation: If no access modifier is specified for a class member in C#, the default access level is 'private'.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The placeholders {0} and {1} in Console.WriteLine correspond to 'name1' and 'address' respectively, producing 'harsh is in new delhi'.

options.text: Creates an object of type csharp on the stack
Declares a reference and creates an object on the heap
Creates a pointer to the address of the class

questions.explanation: In C#, 'csharp abc' declares a reference variable on the stack. 'abc = new csharp()' allocates memory for the actual object on the heap and points the reference to it.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: Compile-time error (Use of unassigned local variable)

questions.explanation: In C#, local variables (like 't' in the Main method) must be assigned a value before they can be used. Since 't' is only declared but not instantiated with 'new test()', it is an unassigned local variable, causing a compile-time error.
